name: FWI (FedWriters, Inc.)
desc:
Transcriptionist | Part-Time | $26-$28/hr
Company: FWI (FedWriters, Inc.)

What Your Day Will Look Like:
You’ll listen to recorded interviews and conversations from federal contracts and type what was said into written transcripts. You’ll follow the project’s formatting and style rules, check the transcript for accuracy, and work with other transcriptionists on quality checks. You’ll check in each day for new files, keep the team updated on your progress, and turn in completed transcripts by the deadline.

What the job is really hiring for: An experienced, accurate legal transcriptionist who can handle sensitive government-related material, meet strict deadlines, and work from detailed style instructions.

Calls and data work:
• Inbound or outbound calls: No customer or sales calls are described in the posting.
• Typing and data entry: Heavy typing is the main work. This is audio transcription and quality review, not general data entry. The posting requires at least 60 WPM.
• Work volume: Intermittent, based on incoming transcription requests; averages 25-50 hours per month.

Actual Minimum Requirements

**Education Minimum:** High school diploma or GED.

**Required Experience:** At least 2 years of transcription experience.

**Preferred Experience:** 5 years of transcription experience; Spanish fluency; court or bank transcription experience.


**Required Skills:**

- Fluent English with strong grammar, vocabulary, and punctuation
- At least 60 words per minute typing speed
- Expert skills in Microsoft Office and MS365 for Web, especially Excel and Word
- Ability to use Windows Media Player or ClipChamp
- Familiarity with legal terminology and legal citation
- Strong communication skills and attention to detail
- Ability to follow style guidance and standard transcription practices
- Ability to meet deadlines and communicate progress
- Ability to pass a background check


**Best Fit:**

**This role is ideal for someone who:**

- Has at least 2 years of transcription experience and strong typing accuracy.
- Knows legal terms and can follow detailed formatting instructions.
- Can work independently, check for errors, and meet deadlines.
- Wants part-time remote work with hours that vary by the volume of assignments.

**Not a Good Fit for someone who:**

- Has less than 2 years of transcription experience.
- Cannot meet the stated typing speed and accuracy expectations.
- Needs steady full-time hours or a predictable workload every week.
- Is uncomfortable working with sensitive federal investigation or interview records.

Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Apply through the employer’s iCIMS job page. The posting does not specify additional application materials or interview stages.
2. The supplied assessment information says applicants must transcribe at 50+ WPM with 100% accuracy. The qualifications section separately requires at least 60 WPM; confirm the required speed with the employer.

Top 10 Resume Keywords:
• Transcription
• Legal transcription
• Legal terminology
• Legal citation
• Grammar and punctuation
• Audio transcription
• Quality checking
• Microsoft Word
• Microsoft Excel
• 60 WPM typing speed

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
• Describe your transcription experience and the types of recordings you have handled.
• How do you make sure a transcript is accurate when the audio is difficult to understand?
• What steps do you take to follow a client's style guide and citation rules?
• How do you organize work when several transcription files have different deadlines?
• What experience do you have handling legal, court, or bank transcription?
